notes: Fixes the container-reported failure: PyTorch was compiled against cuDNN (9,19,0) but the runtime LD_LIBRARY_PATH supplies (9,17,1), so torch.backends.cudnn.is_acceptable raised during model.to('cuda') when the MusicGen decoder LSTM called flatten_parameters. cmd_run now disables the cuDNN backend (torch.backends.cudnn.enabled = False) immediately after verifying CUDA and before loading any model, so _cudnn_is_acceptable short-circuits to False and the version check is never reached; all conv/RNN ops still execute on CUDA via regular kernels (no CPU fallback, no mock weights). The cuDNN state and compiled/runtime version ints are recorded in run.json environment, and a note is added to run.json notes. All other behavior is unchanged: doctor returns 78 on any missing prerequisite and 0 if available without loading weights; --help works without importing torch/transformers; run validates inputs, model config and CUDA before loading, performs greedy text-conditional generation (do_sample=False, guidance_scale=3.0, 200 audio-code tokens for 4 s), writes 32 kHz mono 16-bit WAV per request id under output/music/, re-reads each WAV to verify channels/rate/frames/non-silence/finiteness, and writes output/index.jsonl and output/run.json with input+model references and hashes, parameters, environment, actual durations and GPU-synchronized timings plus peak device memory. Reruns with a new requests.jsonl always regenerate from the model; existing files are never used as the answer. Reference-large melody-conditioned workload remains explicitly not claimed.
